children: France’s TotalEnergies plans to increase its investments in Iraq to $16 billion from $12 billion, as the energy major continues to develop strategic projects in the country, particularly in the gas sector, according to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
TotalEnergies Chairman and CEO Patrick Pouyanné discussed the company’s projects during a meeting with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi in Paris on Monday, the PMO said.
The $10 billion Gas Growth Integrated Project (GGIP) is one of the major projects being developed by the French energy giant in Iraq in partnership with Basra Oil Company and QatarEnergy.
The meeting also covered Iraq’s plans to expand the utilisation of associated gas as it seeks to achieve self-sufficiency.
Al-Zaidi said the government also plans to increase oil production over the next five years, with a target of reaching 10 million barrels per day (bpd).
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
